name: cache-pulse
description: Check static hosting caching for performance: long max-age + immutable on fingerprinted assets, revalidation on HTML, no long cache on unhashed files, Vary and Set-Cookie pitfalls, and precompressed .br/.gz files that match. Reads _headers, vercel.json, netlify.toml, firebase.json. SARIF, Action. Zero deps.

paragraphs: Check that your static hosting config caches the right things: fingerprinted assets for a year, HTML revalidated, and nothing stale after a deploy.

Caching is the cheapest performance win and the easiest to get backwards. Fingerprinted bundles (index-BdT9x2Qa.js) should be cached for a year with immutable; HTML and unfingerprinted files (/styles.css, /logo.png) must revalidate, or visitors keep yesterday's site. cache-pulse reads the header rules in your build output or repo (headers, vercel.json, netlify.toml, firebase.json, serve.json), resolves the Cache-Control that applies to every file, and reports the mistakes, grouped by the header rule that causes them.

CLI, library and GitHub Action. Node.js 18+, zero runtime dependencies. Works on any static build output (Astro, Next.js output: 'export', Eleventy, Hugo, Jekyll, Docusaurus, VitePress, plain HTML) and runs offline: point it at the folder your build writes. By Louis Wright.
features: Fingerprinted assets: content-hashed file names and framework output folders (next/static, astro, app/immutable, nuxt, CRA static/js) need max-age=31536000, immutable; short, missing, no-cache and no-store policies are…
HTML: cached without revalidation or immutable is high severity; s-maxage for the CDN with max-age=0 for browsers is accepted.
Unfingerprinted files: immutable or a max-age over a week on /styles.css or /app.js means users do not see deploys; missing policies are noted.
Pitfalls: Vary: , Set-Cookie on static files (no CDN caching), Content-Encoding on images and fonts.
Compression: when the build ships .br/.gz files, every text asset over 1.4 kB should have one, and each is decompressed and compared with the original to catch stale copies.
